rationale: Wodzicki Definition 2.1 and Encyclopedia of Mathematics U1-U3 state the same proper-filter entourage axioms, quantifiers, and directions; only notation changes.

Wodzicki states that symmetric entourages form a base, and Exercise 23 gives arbitrary finite-composite control. The A4-recovery repair packages those source-backed clauses into one Statement and expands the finite square-root derivation, so the materially repaired Statement is ai-altered and semantically sourced.
Wodzicki defines the uniform topology by exactly the entourage-ball neighborhood condition and proves it is a topology; the item changes notation only.
Both sources define separatedness by the intersection of all entourages being the diagonal, with the same convention and no changed hypothesis.
The sources state the same biconditional for the topology induced by an entourage uniformity. The local proof expands the two directions.
Wodzicki Definition 4.6 and the BIU notes give the same entourage pullback quantifiers for uniform continuity.
Wodzicki states exactly that a uniformly continuous map is continuous in the respective uniform topologies; the item supplies the standard ball proof.

The sources give the metric entourages, induced metric topology, separation, and epsilon-delta interpretation. The item packages these clauses. Unlike the source convention, the library permits an empty metric carrier while requiring filters proper; this creates the empty-carrier defect escalated in A3.

Encyclopedia of Mathematics gives the uniform-cover axioms and Wodzicki develops the associated cover relation. The item uses an equivalent star-refinement presentation and currently overstates equivalence on the empty carrier under the library proper-filter convention.

The sources give the standard equivalence between entourage and uniform-cover formulations. The item spells out both constructions; its cover-to-entourage direction needs the nonempty-carrier qualification recorded for A3.

The sources define a uniformity from finite intersections of pseudometric balls. The item calls the family a gauge and bundles topology and uniform-continuity clauses; under the local proper-filter convention it also needs a nonempty carrier.

ESCALATED TO ALPHA. Iterated symmetric entourage roots are the standard normal-sequence construction in both sources, but the Statement makes the strictly weaker foundational hypothesis DC explicit and no located source states that same choice-calibrated proposition. It is established, not novel; the recursion proof is local. ALPHA CONCURRENCE: Iterating symmetric entourage roots to obtain a decreasing normal sequence with triple-composite control is the classical uniform-space construction. Exposing DC as the recursion principle is a foundational calibration of that standard result, not a novel claim.
Both sources state the normal-sequence metrization lemma with the same dyadic control inclusions and path-infimum pseudometric construction. The proof is a notation-adjusted expansion.

ESCALATED TO ALPHA. The sources prove every uniformity is generated by pseudometrics but assume an ordinary classical background; the item isolates DC as sufficient. The theorem is standard, but no source with the same foundational hypothesis surfaced. ALPHA CONCURRENCE: Representation of an arbitrary uniformity by a family of pseudometrics is a standard uniform-space theorem, and the current proof follows the usual normal-sequence construction. Stating DC as sufficient is an explicit choice calibration, so the local form is established and ai-altered.

ESCALATED TO ALPHA. Literature gives the entourage-cover equivalence and pseudometric generation, but not this exact compound ZF/DC calibration. This is a standard synthesis, not an invented theorem; the proof composes the preceding results. ALPHA CONCURRENCE: Entourage, uniform-cover, and gauge formulations are the standard equivalent presentations of uniform spaces. The nonempty-carrier repair and split ZF/DC bookkeeping adapt the classical package to this library's proper-filter convention without creating new mathematics.
The sources use the same requirement that for every entourage a filter member have square contained in it; notation and equivalent cover wording are the only differences.
Wodzicki Exercise 41 states exactly that every filter convergent in the uniform topology is Cauchy. The item supplies the standard symmetric-root proof, with a missing direct citation proposed at A3.
Wodzicki Exercise 45 states that every adherence point of a Cauchy filter is its convergence point. The proof expands this and needs the induced-topology citation recorded at A3.
Both sources define completeness as convergence of every Cauchy filter, exactly as the item does.
The literature uses the same uniform-isomorphism and subspace-uniformity notions. The item packages the embedding and isomorphism definitions in library notation.

The sources define completion by a complete separated target with dense canonical image and induced original uniformity. The item explicitly permits a noninjective Hausdorff reflection map, the equivalent convention for nonseparated inputs.

Wodzicki 6.1.2-6.1.5 and Hunt give the canonical unique minimal Cauchy filter contained in a Cauchy filter, while Wodzicki 6.1.4-6.1.6 gives the principal-filter instance used by the canonical map. The A4-recovery repair combines those source-backed clauses and supplies the elementary singleton verification, so the materially repaired Statement is ai-altered and semantically sourced.

Wodzicki restricts the standard filter-base uniformity to minimal Cauchy filters and states it is Hausdorff. The item spells out the relation. Its proof omits the nonempty-carrier discharge supplied by the sourced principal-filter clause.
The sources construct the completion from minimal Cauchy filters; completeness of that space is part of the construction. The item isolates and expands that component.

Wodzicki 6.1.6-6.2.4 gives the point-neighborhood-filter map, uniform continuity, and density. The item packages these conclusions; A3 proposes the member-contains-the-point clause actually used later.

The sources state existence of a dense complete Hausdorff completion; Wodzicki also identifies when the canonical map reflects the original uniformity. The item packages the reflection and embedding criterion.
Wodzicki 6.2.3 states the same unique extension of every uniformly continuous map into a complete Hausdorff uniform space. Uniqueness of completions is its exact categorical consequence.

Encyclopedia of Mathematics defines precompactness by finite uniform-cover refinement, equivalently finitely many entourage balls. The item adopts the standard name totally bounded and the entourage formulation.

ESCALATED TO ALPHA. This is the standard ultrafilter characterization behind precompactness, and the finite-cover proof is elementary, but the located Encyclopedia source states only the surrounding completion/precompactness theorem rather than this exact all-ultrafilter proposition. It is established, not novel. ALPHA CONCURRENCE: The finite entourage-ball cover plus ultrafilter primeness argument is the standard proof that every ultrafilter on a totally bounded uniform space is Cauchy. This familiar lemma is established mathematics extracted from the classical compactness equivalence.

ESCALATED TO ALPHA. Compact uniform spaces are standardly complete, and the item gives the usual cluster-point proof, but the located Encyclopedia discussion has already imposed separatedness while this item correctly allows nonseparated uniformities. The broader statement is established but not an exact source match. ALPHA CONCURRENCE: Compact uniform spaces are classically complete via the cluster-point argument for Cauchy filters. Separation is needed for uniqueness, not for existence of a limit, so the nonseparated local convention is a standard broadening rather than a novel result.

ESCALATED TO ALPHA. Compact uniform spaces are standardly totally bounded, with the usual finite entourage-ball subcover proof. The located Encyclopedia statement sits under a separated-uniformity convention, while this item is broader, so the hypothesis delta precludes exact-source treatment. ALPHA CONCURRENCE: The finite-subcover proof from entourage-ball neighbourhoods is the standard theorem that compact uniform spaces are totally bounded. The argument does not require separatedness, making the local convention delta established and mathematically routine.

ESCALATED TO ALPHA. Complete-plus-precompact implies compact is standard, but the item explicitly assumes only the ultrafilter lemma, whereas the source works classically. The local proof verifies that weaker assumption; its extra full-Choice citation is an A3 defect. ALPHA CONCURRENCE: Complete plus totally bounded implies compact is a classical uniform-space theorem. The proof through convergence of ultrafilters uses precisely the ultrafilter lemma; making that weak-choice hypothesis explicit is a standard foundational calibration, not invention.

ESCALATED TO ALPHA. Compact iff complete and totally bounded is standard, but the item records the precise ultrafilter-lemma assumption for the reverse implication. No located source states that same foundational calibration. ALPHA CONCURRENCE: The compactness equivalence is the classical combination of compact-implies-complete, compact-implies-totally-bounded, and the converse. Its explicit ultrafilter-lemma scope is a faithful foundational restatement of established mathematics.
The compact-Hausdorff uniformization proofs in the sources construct finite open refinements with the required star control. The item extracts that standard construction as a named lemma.

The sources construct the unique compatible uniformity on a compact Hausdorff space from diagonal neighborhoods and open covers. The item uses the equivalent cover formulation. Its final entourage recovery fails for the locally admitted empty compact space.

Vienna Theorem 9.4.14 and Wodzicki Corollary 4.8 give uniqueness, with Vienna also giving existence, under the standard nonempty convention. The library admits empty compact Hausdorff space but no uniformity on it, so the exactly-one claim needs nonemptiness.

Wodzicki Theorem 4.7 and BIU state the compact-domain theorem for the natural compatible uniformity. The library convention requires a nonempty domain, and the proof needs the cover dictionary cited explicitly.
The sources define a uniform base by cofinal refinement and countable base exactly as the item does.

ESCALATED TO ALPHA. Decreasing symmetric bases with triple-composite control are the standard metrization normalization, but the item emphasizes its finite-intersection recursion works in ZF. No located source states this exact choice-free proposition. ALPHA CONCURRENCE: Normalizing a countable entourage base to a decreasing symmetric base with triple-composite control is the standard first step in uniform-space metrization. Choosing least indices in a fixed enumeration makes the usual construction choice-free, so the ZF form remains established mathematics.

The sources give pseudometrizability of countably based uniformities and the separated criterion for the pseudometric to distinguish points. The item packages both; its metric criterion needs a direct metric-definition citation.
Wodzicki and Vienna define uniformizable as having a compatible uniformity; the item additionally names the standard separated variant without altering either definition.
The sources state the regularity consequence of a compatible uniformity with the same non-T1 convention. The proof is the standard entourage-shrinking argument.

ESCALATED TO ALPHA. Literature proves uniformizable spaces completely regular via pseudometrics, but the item makes DC explicit as the construction principle. No source with that same foundational hypothesis surfaced. ALPHA CONCURRENCE: The pseudometric-separation proof that uniformizable spaces are completely regular is classical. DC is exposed only to build the normal entourage sequence used by that proof, so the local theorem is an established choice-calibrated version.

Vienna Theorem 9.4.15 and BIU use continuous functions p_f(x,y)=|f(x)-f(y)| to recover the topology. The item makes the gauge explicit; its empty-carrier and triangle-inequality citation defects are escalated.

ESCALATED TO ALPHA. The uniformization theorem is standard, but the biconditional asserts DC suffices and the local definition admits empty completely regular space while proper filters exclude it. No source matches both conventions and hypothesis. ALPHA CONCURRENCE: Uniformizability iff complete regularity under the separation-free convention is a classical theorem. The current nonempty hypothesis resolves the library's proper-filter edge case, and the explicit DC hypothesis records the standard construction's choice cost rather than adding new content.

ESCALATED TO ALPHA. The separated uniformization theorem is standard, but the item exposes DC and the library Tychonoff convention. Empty carrier is currently a counterexample, and T1/Hausdorff bridge citations are incomplete. ALPHA CONCURRENCE: Separated-uniformizable iff Tychonoff is the classical separated form of the uniformization theorem. The repaired nonempty domain, explicit DC, and locally stated T1 convention are recoverable convention and hypothesis adjustments to that standard result.
The BIU notes define a topological group by continuity of multiplication and inversion, exactly matching the item.
The BIU notes state that left and right shifts and inversion are homeomorphisms. The proof expands continuity and inverse formulas.

ESCALATED TO ALPHA. BIU gives exactly these entourage formulas under an explicit Hausdorff hypothesis, while the item correctly defines them for arbitrary, possibly non-Hausdorff topological groups. Dropping Hausdorff is standard established mathematics, but it is a genuine hypothesis delta and no matching source surfaced. ALPHA CONCURRENCE: The displayed left and right entourage formulas are the standard uniformities of a topological group. Their construction uses only the group operations and identity neighbourhoods; Hausdorffness controls separation, not existence, so the broader domain is established.

ESCALATED TO ALPHA. BIU states the natural group uniformities induce the group topology in its Hausdorff uniformity section. The same proof works for arbitrary topological groups and inversion interchanges the two, but no located source states this exact non-Hausdorff package. ALPHA CONCURRENCE: Left and right uniformities inducing the original group topology, with inversion interchanging them, is a standard topological-group theorem. The neighbourhood-translation proof is unchanged without Hausdorffness, so the local package is an established generalization.

ESCALATED TO ALPHA. BIU and Rosendal define the upper join and Roelcke meet with the displayed basic entourages for Hausdorff or Polish groups. The formulas extend unchanged to arbitrary topological groups, a standard convention, but the published domain is broader than the located sources. ALPHA CONCURRENCE: The upper join and Roelcke meet, with intersection and left-right composite bases, are standard topological-group uniformities. The formulas require no separation axiom, so extending their usual sourced domain to arbitrary topological groups is established mathematics.

ESCALATED TO ALPHA. Uniformizability of every topological group and complete regularity of uniformizable spaces are standard, but the item states their precise DC-dependent composition under the non-Hausdorff convention. No source states that exact package. ALPHA CONCURRENCE: Every topological group carries its canonical uniformities, and uniformizable spaces are completely regular in the library's separation-free convention. Their composition, with DC explicitly exposed for the latter implication, is a standard corollary rather than a novel theorem.
BIU defines pointwise convergence from finite coordinate restrictions and uniform convergence from the full coordinate set. The item writes explicit equivalent bases P(F,V) and Q(V).
BIU gives the two bases. Their inclusion and equality when the domain itself is finite are the immediate standard comparison isolated here.
The metric-uniformity construction specializes to the usual absolute-value metric on R and gives its topology and epsilon-delta uniform continuity. The item is that standard specialization.

ESCALATED TO ALPHA. The homeomorphism h(x)=x/(1+|x|) is a standard bounded-coordinate example; searches found only informal exact discussions, not an allowed source for this witness. The verification shows established mathematics, not novelty. Its triangle-inequality citation is wrong. ALPHA CONCURRENCE: The bounded-coordinate homeomorphism x/(1+|x|), its explicit inverse, and the inverse's failure of uniform continuity near the endpoints form a canonical metric/uniform-space example. The current witness is standard and directly recoverable, not AI-invented.

ESCALATED TO ALPHA. Nonuniqueness of compatible uniformities on noncompact spaces is standard; Wodzicki proves uniqueness only compactly and gives continuous-not-uniformly-continuous witnesses. No source states this exact false universal plus pullback refutation. ALPHA CONCURRENCE: A topology need not determine a unique compatible uniformity, and pulling back the interval's metric uniformity along the canonical homeomorphism gives the standard counterexample mechanism. The local false-statement package is established mathematics.

ESCALATED TO ALPHA. The sourced group formulas and commutativity make all four group uniformities equal the usual metric uniformity on additive R. No source states this exact four-way example, but it is standard, not novel. ALPHA CONCURRENCE: In an abelian topological group the left and right uniformities coincide, so their upper join and Roelcke meet coincide as well; on additive R the common entourages are exactly the usual metric ones. This is a canonical worked instance of standard definitions.

ESCALATED TO ALPHA. Moving-tail indicator functions are a canonical pointwise-not-uniform witness, but no reputable source with this exact N-to-{0,1} construction surfaced. The verification is direct and established; its discrete-uniformity citation is incomplete. ALPHA CONCURRENCE: Moving-tail indicator functions on N are a canonical example separating pointwise from uniform convergence: every coordinate is eventually zero while each function still attains one. The zero-one target uniformity makes the standard witness exact.
Vienna Theorem 9.4.14 gives the unique compatible uniformity on every compact Hausdorff space, and the metric construction identifies it on [0,1]. The item is this standard specialization.

ESCALATED TO ALPHA. ETSU notes prove the K-topology Hausdorff but not regular, while uniformizable spaces are regular. Their composition gives this conclusion, but no source states it as one proposition; it is standard, not novel. ALPHA CONCURRENCE: The K-topology is the classical Hausdorff nonregular example, and every uniformizable space is regular under the library's convention. Composing those established results gives the standard nonuniformizability counterexample directly.
